independent.summary: citeAnchor never uses the absorbed anchor when the receiving chunk has its own [H2] header, so the headline failure the item describes — a retrieval hit on the appended trailing text deep-linking to the *preceding* section — is unchanged from main. The branch reduces to `sectionAnchor || extras[0]`: whenever `sectionAnchor` exists (the canonical merged case, test D) `extraAnchors` has zero effect on the citation, despite the item asking the builder to 'prefer the anchor whose heading text actually appears in the matched chunk' (the absorbed [H2] text does appear, in the body).

In the one case the change does alter — an anchorless receiving chunk — it can introduce a new wrong anchor where main cited none. The absorbed section is by construction under TINY_BUF_THRESHOLD (<200 chars) while the receiving intro body runs toward CHUNK_TARGET (~1200+, see test E: ~1300 vs 136), so most of the chunk's text does *not* sit under the absorbed heading; a hit on the intro now cites `url#office` and jumps the visitor past the matched content, whereas the previous bare URL landed them at the top of the page where that intro actually is.
